zones.what: Deck 8 (Favola) is the lowest balcony deck and sits at the lifeboat/davit line; specific balcony cabins there (port 8071+, starboard 8070+, plus 8240/8244/8245/8249) have solid-metal balcony fronts up to railing height, and deck 9's indented balconies (port 9147-9161, starboard 9148-9162) look down onto the tops of the lifeboats.
zones.effect: On deck 8 the metal-fronted cabins can't see out at all while seated; on deck 9 you can't look straight down at the sea but the outward horizon view is unaffected.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to anyone who wants to watch the water from a lounger; doesn't matter to people who mainly care about the horizon view or who plan to stand at the rail.
zones.source: cruisedeckplans.com deck-by-deck pages for MSC Fantasia decks 8 and 9, cross-checked against identical cabin numbering on sister ship MSC Splendida's deck 8/10 pages; MSC's own deck-plan PDF legend also codes 'Balcony with metal balustrade' and 'obstructed view' categories for this class

zones.what: CruiseMapper notes that some MSC Yacht Club Deluxe Suites (YC1) on decks 15-16 have partially obstructed views due to lifeboat interference.
zones.effect: A subset of top-deck Yacht Club suites can have a lifeboat or related structure intrude on the view despite being far above the actual lifeboat deck.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to Yacht Club guests paying suite prices who expect an unobstructed view; MSC does not label which specific YC1 cabins are affected in public materials.
zones.source: cruisemapper.com MSC Fantasia cabins page: 'some YC1-Deluxe Suites have partially obstructed views (lifeboat interference)'

zones.what: Deck 13 (Arcobaleno, all guest cabins) sits directly beneath deck 14 (Miraggio), which holds the main Lido pool, Aqua Park, the Zanzibar and L'Africana buffet restaurants, and the Aurea Spa.
zones.effect: Deck 13 cabins can pick up noise from lounger-dragging, pool splash activity, and buffet service traffic directly overhead.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to light sleepers or anyone planning a lie-in; doesn't matter much to families who want to be one flight from the pool.
zones.source: cruisedeckplans.com MSC Fantasia deck 13 page: 'All cabins on this deck are below public areas on the deck above and may experience noise issues'; cruisemapper.com deck 14 plan confirms deck 14 is Lido-Pools-Spa with the two main buffets

zones.what: Deck 12 (Incanto) is sandwiched between deck 11 and deck 13, both entirely guest-cabin decks with no public venues.
zones.effect: Cabins on deck 12 tend to have quieter neighbours above and below since there is no venue-generated noise from either direction.
zones.mattersTo: Good pick for noise-sensitive guests; irrelevant to guests who don't care about ambient noise.
zones.source: cruisedeckplans.com MSC Fantasia deck 12 page: 'The cabins on this deck are above and below decks with only cabins on them...less noise issues from public areas'

zones.what: Decks 6 and 7 below deck 8 carry no cabins and are given over to public venues (theatre, dining, atrium-level spaces); deck 8 cabins sit directly above that public-venue stack.
zones.effect: Deck 8 guests can pick up structure-borne noise from theatre or restaurant activity on the deck below, on top of the lifeboat-line effects already noted for that deck.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to guests booking deck 8 for the lower balcony price point; less relevant to those on higher decks.
zones.source: cruisedeckplans.com MSC Splendida deck 8 page (identical hull/cabin numbering to Fantasia): 'All cabins on this deck are above public areas on the deck below'

zones.what: As the hull narrows on higher decks, balconies on decks 9 (cabins 9147-9161 port/9148-9162 starboard), 12 and 13 are indented/set back from the hull edge, so looking straight down shows the tops of lifeboats or ship structure several decks below (2 decks below on deck 9, 4 on deck 12, 5 on deck 13) rather than the sea.
zones.effect: You lose the straight-down view of the water and get a shaded, overhung balcony (especially on deck 13, where aft-facing balconies shrink to a narrow Juliet-style ledge), but the outward horizon view remains good.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to guests who like to watch the waterline directly below; doesn't matter to those who care mainly about the outward sea view or sunset.
zones.source: cruisedeckplans.com MSC Fantasia deck 9, 12 and 13 pages describing indented balconies viewing 'the top of lifeboats X decks below' and deck 13's 'large overhang' and 'very small Juliett style balcony' on aft-facing cabins

zones.what: Aft hull-design balcony cabins on deck 8 (e.g. 8249) sit low and near the stern machinery spaces.
zones.effect: A guest in cabin 8249 reported constant engine noise and tremors through most of the sailing.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to light sleepers or anyone sensitive to vibration; less relevant to guests who sleep through anything.
zones.source: seascanner.com guest review of MSC Fantasia cabin 8249: 'a lot of noise and tremors from the ship's engines most of the time of sailing'; corroborated by a Cruise Critic thread asking about vibration/motor noise on Fantasia-class deck 8 aft cabins

zones.what: Elevator lobbies on this class draw heavy foot traffic; a first-person reviewer called the lifts 'a nightmare' at peak times, while another guest specifically chose a deck 11 cabin (11191) for its proximity to a lift bank.
zones.effect: Being near a lift bank cuts your walk but adds door-chime and hallway-traffic noise and lift-queue congestion at peak times (meal times, disembarkation).
zones.mattersTo: Convenience-focused guests and those with mobility needs benefit; noise-sensitive guests should ask for a cabin a few doors away from the lobby rather than adjacent to it.
zones.source: tripadvisor.com MSC Fantasia review: 'The lifts are a bit of a nightmare...really slow at peak times... Our balcony cabin was on deck 11 and ideally located for the lift, cabin number 11191'

zones.what: This class offers 'Super-Family' and cluster cabin categories that let 2-3 cabins be joined by a connecting door, and MSC's own deck-plan legend marks these connecting-cabin pairs throughout the balcony categories.
zones.effect: Great for families/groups wanting adjoining space, but the connecting door is a weaker sound barrier than a standard cabin wall, so if only one side is booked you'll hear more from next door than usual.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to groups wanting linked cabins (a plus) and to solo/couple bookers who end up next to an unrelated connecting pair (a minus).
zones.source: cruisemapper.com MSC Fantasia cabins page on 'Super-Family' and interconnecting 'cluster cabins'; msc's official deck-plan PDF legend marks 'Connecting cabins'; cruisemummy.co.uk notes the connecting door 'does a worse job of soundproofing than a regular wall'
